what: IndexedDB is the browser's built-in database for large, structured data: objects, files and blobs, with indexes and transactions. It is asynchronous, so it does not freeze the page, and it is the right place for offline data and queues.
like: Like a filing cabinet in the classroom with labelled drawers and index cards: you can store a lot, find things by label, and the work is done by a helper so you are never blocked.
why: Stores far more than localStorage without blocking the UI
Indexes and transactions give fast lookups and safe updates
Works from the page, workers and service workers, so offline data is shared

steps.d: indexedDB.open(name, version) returns a request. Schema changes happen only in onupgradeneeded: create object stores and indexes there.
An object store is like a table of objects, with a keyPath or auto-generated key. Add indexes for the fields you query, for example by date or status.
Every read and write happens in a transaction on named stores. It commits when its pending requests finish; do not await unrelated things inside it.
The raw API is event-based, so teams use a promise wrapper: idb for a thin layer, Dexie for schema, queries and live updates.
Pages, workers and service workers on the same origin see the same data. Ask for persistent storage for important data and catch QuotaExceededError.

numbers.l: of total disk a Chromium or Safari origin can use at most (Firefox best-effort: 10% of disk or 10 GiB)
Web Storage limit per origin - the small box IndexedDB replaces
readwrite transaction can run on an object store at a time, so keep them short

choices.d: web.dev suggests Cache Storage for network resources, OPFS for file-like content and IndexedDB for other structured data. Avoid localStorage for anything big because it is synchronous.
The raw API is verbose and event-based. idb adds promises with little else; Dexie adds a declarative schema, a query API and live queries.
Integer versions with onupgradeneeded migrations. Plan how to migrate each older version, and handle other tabs blocking an upgrade.
Data is best-effort by default. Call navigator.storage.persist() for important data, check estimate(), and catch QuotaExceededError.

instead.why: For tiny settings like a theme, where a synchronous key-value store is enough
When the data you need to keep is a queue of pending actions, built on top of IndexedDB

breaks.d: An old tab keeps the previous version open, so the new version waits.
breaks.see: Database never opens after a deploy
breaks.fix: Close the connection in onversionchange and show a 'please reload' message on blocked

breaks.d: Awaiting a fetch or timer inside a transaction lets it auto-complete.
breaks.fix: Fetch first, then open a short transaction and only await IndexedDB requests inside

breaks.d: The disk is full or the browser clears best-effort data.
breaks.see: Writes throw QuotaExceededError, or data vanishes
breaks.fix: try/catch writes, trim old data, request persistent storage, and treat the server as the source of truth

say: For anything bigger than a few settings I use IndexedDB: asynchronous, transactional, with indexes, and available in workers and service workers.
I wrap it with idb or Dexie, version the schema with migrations in onupgradeneeded, and keep transactions short.
I treat it as a cache of server data - request persistent storage for the important parts and handle QuotaExceededError.

followups.a: It is synchronous so it blocks the main thread, holds only strings, is limited to about 5 MiB, and is not available in workers.

followups.q: Is IndexedDB data guaranteed to stay?
followups.a: No. It is best-effort and can be evicted under storage pressure; navigator.storage.persist() asks for protection, and Safari can clear script-written data after 7 days without interaction.

followups.q: How do you migrate the schema?
followups.a: Bump the integer version; in onupgradeneeded create or change stores and indexes, branching on the old version. It is the only place schema can change.

today: IndexedDB is the standard store for structured offline data, usually behind a wrapper: idb for promises or Dexie for schema and live queries (Dexie Cloud adds sync). The origin private file system covers file-style content, and persistent storage requests protect critical data.

check.q: Where can the schema of an IndexedDB database change?
check.why: Stores and indexes are created or deleted only during a version upgrade.

check.q: Why avoid localStorage for large offline data?
check.a: It is synchronous and blocks the main thread
check.why: It also holds only strings and about 5 MiB.

check.q: A write throws QuotaExceededError. What do you do?
check.a: Catch it, free space and retry or degrade gracefully
check.why: MDN recommends wrapping writes in try/catch and freeing space.
